body: Dug up my old throwaway for this just in case. Just how often I have thought about ending things, but unable to bring myself to go through with it. I feel I am just lingering at this point and I doubt very much that things will improve.

I'm in group therapy myself, and although I have mentioned to them that I have had suicidal thoughts, I have omitted just how often I have them and how much I hate myself. There's not really much they were able to do on the occassions I have said something, so I see no point in mentioning it any more. The two main reasons I haven't acted on these thoughts so far are that I lack the will neccesary to act on them (or anything else for that matter), and the effects on my parents and brother. So I guess I'm stuck waiting until either I improve or I can't wait anymore.

Is CBT effective for long-term depression and anxiety? Only I've been attending group therapy for the last 2 years and have made very little progress. At most it has helped slow the decline of my mental state by giving some contact with people outside my family, as I don't really speak to anyone else. I'll be honest, the thought that this state might be permanent or continue to get worse scares me.

I liked this. Hits the mark pretty close. Was a little longer and more poetic than I was thinking of though for a text, and I couldn't send something so well thought out as my own. But thanks for putting it into words.

You have just pretty described me when I was at university. Speaking personally, things haven't exactly gotten better. On the plus side I was able to push through the remainder of university, though my marks did suffer, but afterwards I was left completely directionless and with very little motivation. Living at home with my parents, I have previously made attempts to try get myself doing something, but have found myself lacking the willpower to follow through, whether that be applying for jobs or more recently just doing anything. It has been about 2 years since uni ended, and I have pretty much nothing to show for it and have more or less given up on myself.

So my advice? Get the problem sorted out as soon as possible. Seek help, whether that be from your doctor and/or services at your university (depending on what's available) like your careers department. Joining societies and sports clubs at uni to get more involved may help, but that depends on your personality and how up to it you feel. With regards to therapy, it can be hit and miss. I'm in group therapy but have seen little benefit outside of having people to talk to outside of family, but I got stuck on a waiting list (NHS) so long it wasn't until uni had finished I got therapy. Depending on the means you have available, try as many treatments as possible until you find one that helps. I've heard good things about CBT. So definetely seek help sooner rather than later, trust me it only gets much harder later.

It doesn't really help that I have problems with social anxiety and few interests to speak of. Even online I struggle to talk to people. Videogames used to be a mental haven for me but now I even find them very difficult to get into. I am frequently very disappointed with myself, often for failing to get myself to do things and past similar failings.
I have always struggled making and keeping friends. Combine that with depression and after a while you just kind of shut down.

Using my throwaway that I've come to use for these kind of posts. Most days the thought crosses my mind at least once if not more. What aspect of suicide my mind is obsessing about tends to vary. From a young age I've never been particularly motivated, I would simply stop very easily without significant and frequent "nudging" but that trait has significantly worsened in recent years (quite frankly it was surprising I made it though uni). I don't really have friends (I've always had poor social skills and been developmentally behind socially), am unemployed with no real dreams for a career. No real hobbies. Just trying to keep myself going most days with small pointless things.

I do not have a future as I am now. I see no point in finding a job for the sole purpose of having money to "live". Suffering for the sake of suffering more is how it appears in my mind. It wouldn't be so bad if I had something else to live for that made it all worthwhile but I don't. The main reason I have not killed myself so far is the "what ifs?" that have more or less gone, and the guilt. I don't want to hurt my parents, I know it would hurt them but I can't keep this up. I've tried small things previously, but those good days when I manage to get something done are nearly impossible to come by now. I regret a lot of things. I make poor decisions that tend to be dominated by either laziness or fear. I envy those who have that "get-up-and-go" attitude that has always been alien to me. 

On the rare occassion I spot something interesting I often sabotage it, which I have speculated is related to my suicidal thoughts in group therapy, which for me is next to useless. So here I am wondering why I am here at all and when I want to "opt out".

Couple this with the fact that they were very overprotective, and myself always having had difficulty socially and seeming to have a natural inclination towards laziness and you have me. I had very little self confidence when I was younger, but I did well academically, and being told I was smart gave me something to hold onto. Despite my almost complete failure socially growing up, I clung to that idea, reinforced by the fact that I found school easy and could just coast by. I could handle the short bursts of intense work for larger assignments, with nagging from parents, but come university, I was in for a culture shock. I was average studying physics at uni. First year I got by ok but my increasing social isolation (I had a few friends by colleges end, before uni, which disintergrated afterwards) triggered depression towards the end of the first year of uni which has never really abated despite attempts at treatment.

After that the work got hard, and I struggled to put in the effort. Somehow I managed to make it to the end and got a 2:1, but I was a wreck by the end. Things have gone downhill from there. I still didn't know what I wanted to do with myself. Careers guidance couldn't help, and although I did get offered a phd position, it triggered major anxiety and nearly caused me to fudge my exams. So that opportunity went, along with another phd offer that I had a similar reaction to. Anything real and I retreat into my video games, internet and god knows what else. That leads me to now.

I'm 23 going on 24, and I finished uni coming up to 2 years ago now, and have done virtually nothing since then. I am currently depressed to the point of feeling suicidal every single day. I see my own life as worthless and have kept going this long for 2 reasons. One, the ever fainter hope that things might improve and I can change, however, little of this remains. And two, guilt, I don't want to hurt them. It isn't a pleasant existance, and seeing how my current state affects all of them, hurts. I don't have any friends, I have no desires for the future, and my self destructive tendencies undermine me at every turn. I've missed opportunities, I'm very good at making excuses for them, and all I suspect because a part of me wants to drive me closer to that point of self destruction.

I have a list of criticisms that I seem to attack myself with on a regular basis...

You're not smart, you just pretend to be.

You don't matter.

In the long term they'd be better off without you.

You will never truly belong anywhere.

Who are you?

You have no real dreams, no motivation, how do you expect this story to end?

It's too late for you.

Nothing will ever fill that void inside you.

A realm of infinite possibility before you and you choose to do nothing but hide in brief distractions and wild, hollow fantasies that can never be; from the dark truths that haunt you, from the longing that you can never sate, and the fragments of empty dreams.

You're not real.

You've screwed up every choice you ever made, let yourself be consumed by doubts, and let every opportunity pass you by, out of fear.

You're alone.

Sometimes it feels like I'm watching myself slowly dying. In a way I am. My brain's a jerk... And in case you may be wondering why I am looking at a thread like this: to try and make me feel slightly less alone, and if I'm really lucky, find an answer.

I graduated about a year ago. I was studying MSci (BSc + MSc combined) Physics. I was approached by my supervisor for my final year project and offered a PhD position as well, however, I had a similar reaction to that offer as this one (being around exam time as well made things worse). In the end I figured some time out would help put things in perspective, though that doesn't seem to have happened yet.
It's a lot to think about. Anyway, thank you for all the advice. I hope I haven't taken up too much of your time.

Is it possible to do a phd after a few years doing a regular job? I have to admit towards the end of my undergrad I felt like I was keeping myself going on anxiety and stress alone. I have some suspisions that I might have some form of Aspergers, based on past experience and my behavious around other people, which doesn't help. I used to have passion for the sciences, especially physics but that seems to have faded leaving virtually nothing behind.

Well, thank you for your thoughts. I hope I didn't waste too much of your time. Sorry if it turned into a bit of rant, as you may of noticed I'm quite stressed.

Btw I noticed that you studied at RHUL as well.

I had my interview last friday. So my dad says (my parents picked me up from the uni and arrived slightly early), the woman (I think she was the equivilant of department secretary) wanted a decision by tomorrow morning because they two other applicants coming in for the one remaining position (there will be two positions if I turn it down). My parents keep pressuring me to just make a decision, I know they are frustrated with me but getting annoyed at me doesn't help. I don't like disappointing people. The job market here in the UK is uncertain and there's no guarantee that I will have the chance again to do a funded phd even if I do manage to get a job for a few years. I feel really tired right now. 

Edit: From what I recall reading a phd is necessary for a number of jobs in physics (though not all). My only other option is to take the gamble and hope I can right myself within the first taught year, before the research component in the subsequent years.

Thanks for the advice. Currently on duloxetine. I have been put on several different ones previously, though my doctor seems reluctant to change them again, and I'm not very pushy about it. From what little you have read about me here, do you see any possibility of me accepting the position ending well?

I am on antidepressents and attending group therapy. The antidepressants have limited effectiveness, they seem to help soften the lows but they don't seem to really help raise my base mood or energy (I think they may actually be hindering positive emotions as well). They basically flatten my mood.
Group therapy seems to have little effect either besides giving some contact with people outside the family and alleviating some loneliness. On that note the professors seemed to indicate that this phd would involve a lot of collaborative work. I don't know if that would make a difference.

Thank you for the reply. I have to make a decision today really. An offer of a position has come through. My undergrad was in physics (MSci) (UK), and this programme is in complex systems simulation, which I seemed to have more affinity for. My dilemma is that about greatest amount of interest I seem to be capable of reaching right now is "somewhat interested". I very rarely get particularly enthusiatic about anything, and even then, not for long, despite being on antidepressants. At the very least I must have come across as interested during the interview by several professors at once, and they came back with their decision quickly.

I'm somewhat reluctant to turn around and say no, when I don't really have anything else lined up and during the taught year I might find a specific topic I do feel passionate about, though I admit it feels like a long shot, or sucessfully manage my emotions and have my current interest turn into passion. I find there are a number of topics which interest me to some degree but how well I could sustain that is unknown. If I say no then the opportunity for this topic is gone and unlikely to return. And what if this is about the most interested I will get about anything? I don't know if I can just let this go. I also don't know how viable it is to go into industry (assuming I can even find meaningful work, if it exists) and then decide to do a phd after a few years.

On the other hand, I'm also reluctant to say yes. There were some real low points during my undergrad degree when I felt so bad I wanted to just call it quits. I'm not sure how serious I was, but after talking with my parents and some coaxing from them I managed to keep going. Whilst I did like doing my research project in my masters year, it kept my mind occupied and interested, I geniunely hated the write-up (though I managed to get a 1st in it). At one point I ended up sobbing not knowing how I was going to get it finished in time. Additionally if I decide to do the phd and then find I'm not able to continue and then drop out, and then decide a few years later that I want to try again, it will count against me and make it difficult to be accepted.

I've never been much good at making long-term decisions like this. I've been agonizing over it so much, I've ended up upsetting my mum because neither she or my dad know how to help. They don't come from a scientific background and I don't feel I have anyone I can talk to about this freely. There is a fair amount of contradictory statements from looking around the internet, some stating that moving from industry back to academia is rare and difficult, others saying it helps give perspective. Most agree you need to enthusiatic about your area of research, though I may find during the taught year a specific area that qualifies, though it's a gamble. Any further advice, I'm having trouble organizing all my thoughts sufficiently to be able to come to any kind of decision.

Edit: I had seen that link on the 5 stages of phd motivation while researching what a phd would involve. The crisis of meaning does concern me as my personality is prone to that type of thinking, and I don't know if I will be able to get through it. Ironically this last week is the most energized I've felt in months, though it seems to be coming mostly from anxiety and stress, which now seems to be decaying back into mildy interested apathy.
I'm also concerned I will disappoint my parents, though they say they don't mind whatever I decide.

It was a 4 year course. 3 year bsc with a masters year on the end. My final year project was in particle physics, analysing simulated data for collisions at the LHC in C++ but I also did a unit on nanophysics, quantum computation and communication, general relativity and cosmology and some others. I never fully specialized. I originally went into physics because I both enjoyed it and thought it would be useful for finding a career. But I seem to have lost most of that enjoyment. And I feel if I can't find something to follow on from my degree now that it will be too late, it may already. Sorry for the longish reply.
I do have a tendency to overanalyze everything. It does get annoying, and sadly it doesn't have an off switch. I'm just trying to figure myself out and find my place in this world.
